weeks.title: Seeking God’s Will
weeks.theme: God’s will is not a blueprint; it is following the Shepherd step by step with a renewed mind.
group: Rom 12:1–2 says that before we prove God’s will, which two things come first?
When I sought God’s will in the past, did I mostly want an answer, or did I want to know the God who guides?
Which decision this week am I willing to entrust to God first, and ask my group members to pray along with me?
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday gathering, find a trusted companion and take two minutes to say, “Something I’m waiting on God to guide me in right now is…” The other person doesn’t give answers; you simply pray quietly together for three minutes. Then send one sentence to a friend: “God’s guidance is often found in a renewed mind.”
weeks.weekend: This weekend, set aside a half day of “quiet listening”: turn off notifications first, and take a notebook and your Bible to a quiet place. Read Rom 12:1–2 and write down one thing you need to entrust to God; then spend twenty minutes in silence. Afterward, share with a companion what you heard and which step you can take right now.

lessons.title: Do Not Be Conformed to This World
lessons.hear:
When Xiaowen was deciding whether to accept a job in another city, she asked everyone around her for their opinion, but she never quietly asked God. Only later did she realize that what she wanted was not God’s will but someone to carry the consequences of the decision for her.

Paul says in Romans, “Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.” (Rom 12:2) Notice the order: first presenting yourself, then the renewing of your mind, and only then proving God’s will.

God’s will is not an answer handed over first and then you are asked to believe it; first there is a renewed heart, and then you can see what God sees. This world teaches us to decide by conditions, feelings, and immediate gain, but God wants us to see through his eyes.

Proving God’s will is a process, not a drawing of lots.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he offered himself to the Father and lived his whole life doing only what pleased the Father. The Bible is my standard: don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he renews my mind so that I can see the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God. People who live for self demand answers from God; people who live in selflessness first offer themselves and let Jesus be King.
think: According to Rom 12:2, after we stop being conformed to the world, what are we transformed by?
When I make decisions now, what do I mainly rely on: my feelings, other people, or God’s word?
Today, how can I change my attitude toward a decision from “wanting an answer” to “offering myself”?
lessons.speak: Lord, I offer myself to you and will not be conformed to this world. Holy Spirit, renew my mind, so that I look at things not by my feelings and immediate gain but through your eyes. Let me first know you, and then know your will. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, before you make any choice, pause for thirty seconds and say to God, “Lord, I give this to you.” Write down in your journal the one decision you most want to make today.
lessons.quick: God’s will is not about asking for an answer first, but about offering yourself first.
text: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

lessons.title: I Will Instruct You and Teach You
lessons.hear:
After his breakup, Zhe kept wanting to know whether God had arranged someone for him. He prayed every day, but the more he prayed, the more restless he became.

The psalm says, “I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.” (Ps 32:8) The point of this verse is that God says “I”: I will instruct, I will teach, I will counsel you with my eye on you.

God’s guidance is not handing you a map and walking away; he himself walks with you and keeps his eye on you. Because his eye is on you, he will not miss any of your turns.

You don’t have to guess desperately in the dark, because the one guiding you is the God who loves you. All you need to do is stay within his sight.

Today, take “you have your eye on me” as a starting point: you are not someone left by the roadside, but someone God watches over all the time.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he often withdrew to the wilderness to pray and moved forward under the Father’s eye. The Bible is my standard: I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he will teach us all things. People who live for self want to hold the road in their own hands; people who live in selflessness walk with peace under God’s eye.
think: In Ps 32:8, what things does God say he will do for me?
Do I often think of God’s guidance as something hidden and hard to catch?
How can I come closer to God’s sight today, instead of rushing to find the answer myself?
lessons.speak: Heavenly Father, thank you for saying that you will instruct me and keep your eye on me. Forgive me for so often being anxious and searching desperately for answers on my own. Quiet me, help me know that you are always watching over me, and lead me in the way I should go. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, spend five minutes meditating on Ps 32:8, and write the words “you have your eye on me” in a note on your phone. Read it each time you feel anxious.
lessons.quick: God doesn’t only show the way; he walks with you and keeps his eye on you.
text: I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.

lessons.title: This Is the Way; Walk in It
lessons.hear:
Xiaolan struggled for a long time between two choices, yet she never heard any voice. She felt she must not be spiritual enough.

Isaiah says, “and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, ‘This is the way. Walk in it.’” (Isa 30:21) There are two details here. First, the voice is “behind you,” which means that after you have already taken a step, God speaks up along the road. Second, the voice says “walk in it,” not “think it through before you go.”

Many people wait for a voice until they are afraid to move. But God often corrects your direction while you are walking.

So conviction is not waiting until everything is clear before acting. It is taking a small step that does not go against God’s word, with the help of prayer, the Bible, and companions, and trusting that he will speak to you along the way.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: at every step he walked in the way the Father showed him. The Bible is my standard: this is the way; walk in it. The Holy Spirit is my guide: along the road he reminds, corrects, and confirms. People who live for self want to see everything before they will walk; people who live in selflessness are willing to take the first step.
think: In Isa 30:21, is the voice in front of the person or behind? What does this tell me?
Am I hesitating to take that step because I want to be completely sure?
What small step that doesn’t go against the Bible can I take first today?
lessons.speak: Lord, I often wait until everything is clear before I dare to move. Forgive my hesitation. Make me willing to take the first step, and help me trust that you will remind and correct me along the way. I want to walk in the right way you show me. Give me peace, too, so that I am not bound by fear. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, choose one small thing that you have put off for a long time and that does not go against the Bible, and do it now: send a message, sign up for an event, or finish a form. When you are done, give thanks to God.
lessons.quick: God often speaks from behind to show direction while you are walking.
text: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”

lessons.title: Commit Your Deeds to the LORD
lessons.hear:
Before taking a relationship with someone a step further, Xun made a very long list: qualities, pros and cons, risks. He said this was what being responsible meant.

Being responsible is right, but Proverbs says, “Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.” (Prov 16:3) To commit does not mean to stop planning; it means to place your plans in God’s hands.

The original sense of “commit” here is something like rolling a heavy burden onto someone else. You do what you should do: pray, read the Bible, ask your companions, assess reality; then you give the outcome, and your heart, to God.

Note that “shall succeed” is not a guarantee of the outcome you want. It is a guarantee that when you give your plans to God, his good purpose will be established, and that is often better than our original plans.

Today, try to really hand over the one thing you find hardest to let go of.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: in Gethsemane he said, not my will, but yours. The Bible is my standard: commit your deeds to the LORD. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps us let go and rest. People who live for self cling to the outcome; people who live in selflessness do their part and leave the outcome to God.
think: What does Prov 16:3 say will happen after we commit our deeds?
Do I “give my plans to God,” or do I only ask God to stamp them after they are finished?
What is the one thing I will commit to him today? How can I do that in a concrete way?
lessons.speak: God, I commit to you what I do and what I plan. I am willing to do my part, but I place the outcome in your hands. Quiet my heart, and let your good purpose be established in me. Give me patience to wait, too. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write down one thing you are planning, and under it write: My part is…; what I commit to God is… Then pray aloud, and put the paper in your Bible.
lessons.quick: Do your part, and leave the outcome to God.
text: Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.

lessons.title: My Sheep Hear My Voice
lessons.hear:
Look back on this week: God’s will begins with offering ourselves and a renewed mind (Rom 12:2); God instructs us and keeps his eye on us (Ps 32:8); along the way he reminds us of the direction (Isa 30:21); we commit what we do to him (Prov 16:3).

Jesus said, “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.” (John 10:27) Sheep don’t follow by reading a map; they follow by knowing the shepherd’s voice. Familiarity comes from daily presence.

So the most important lesson in seeking God’s will is not a technique but a relationship. The better you know him, the better you can tell which is his voice and which is your own fear, desire, or someone else’s pressure.

Ask yourself: Where did I see my self-centeredness this week? How did God hold me up in the middle of it?

This week’s lesson will not be wasted, because knowing the Shepherd is a lifelong matter.
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he is the good shepherd who knows his sheep. The Bible is my standard; every voice is confirmed by God’s word. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he makes us familiar with the Lord’s voice. The order of relationships: first God, then self, others, and things. Let Jesus be King, and give all the glory to God.
think: According to John 10:27, how do the sheep follow the shepherd?
Where did I see my self-centeredness this week (rushing for answers, clinging to outcomes)? How did God hold me up in the middle of it?
What is one thing I will keep doing so that I become more familiar with the Lord’s voice?
lessons.speak: Jesus, my good Shepherd, thank you for knowing me. Help me become more familiar with your voice each day, and tell the difference between your words and my own fears and desires. I want to follow you. All glory to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Write in your journal: my biggest discovery this week; where my self-centeredness showed up; and one habit I will keep. Then set aside the first ten minutes of today for God.
lessons.quick: Knowing the Shepherd’s voice comes from his daily presence.
text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

weeks.keyText: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.

weeks.title: Looking to Jesus Together
weeks.theme: For two people to go far, they don’t gaze at each other; they look to Jesus together.
group: Heb 12:2 says whom we are to look to. What did he do for our faith?
In my past or present relationships, are we gazing at each other, or looking to Jesus together?
With which companion can I set aside a time this week to draw near to God together?
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday gathering, find a companion or friend and write down together three things “we want to look to God for together,” and pray for each other. Then send one sentence to a friend: “A good relationship is two people facing the same God.”
weeks.weekend: This weekend, do one thing that “faces the same direction” with a companion, friend, or small group: read a passage of Scripture together, serve someone together, or pray together for a need. When you finish, each say one sentence: What did this help me know about God?

lessons.title: Looking to Jesus, the Author and Perfecter of Faith
lessons.hear:
When Xiaokai and his girlfriend were dating, the two of them were always face to face, watching each other’s reactions, moods, and how fast they replied. After a while, both felt exhausted.

Hebrews says, “looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith.” (Heb 12:2) Jesus is the author of faith, who opened the way; he is also the perfecter, who will surely lead us to the end.

If two people only look at each other, every imperfection gets magnified; but if they look to Jesus together, they have a shared direction and a shared strength.

The cloud of witnesses surrounding us is a reminder that we are not the first to walk this road. You can lay aside the weight and the sin that entangles, because there are people on the road, and the Lord is there too. Looking to Jesus is the best starting point for a relationship.

Today, start with one simple question: Whom am I looking at right now?
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he endured the suffering of the cross for us and sat down at the right hand of God. The Bible is my standard: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he turns our eyes from each other to Jesus. People who live for self stare at the other person; people who live in selflessness look to the Lord together with a companion.
think: What does Heb 12:2 say Jesus did for our faith?
In relationships, do I more often look at the other person or at Jesus?
Today, how can I turn my eyes from the other person’s performance to Jesus?
lessons.speak: Jesus, you are the author and perfecter of my faith. Forgive me for so often staring at people and at myself. Turn my eyes to you, and in my relationships help me look to you together with my companions. I will follow you all the way to the end. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, when you think of someone important to you, don’t start by worrying about their reaction. First spend two minutes looking to Jesus, and offer thanks to the Lord and entrust this person and this relationship to him.
lessons.quick: A good relationship is two people looking to Jesus together.
text: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

lessons.title: A Threefold Cord Is Not Quickly Broken
lessons.hear:
Hong and Ling decided to start dating, but they always felt the relationship was fragile: every time they argued, it felt as if it would snap. They asked an older mentor, who said only one thing: “Your cord has only two strands.”

Ecclesiastes says, “a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (Eccl 4:12) This line is often used as an illustration for marriage, but its meaning is broader: for any relationship to be strong, it needs a third strand, who is God.

The third strand is not a formality but a real presence: each person has an intimate relationship with God, and together they open themselves to God. When the relationship faces pressure, instead of each clinging to the other, they hold on to God together.

This also reminds us that besides the two of you, you need spiritual companions and elders to weave the cord tighter.

Will you start today by inviting God to be the third strand between you?
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he was one with the Father and also walked with his disciples. The Bible is my standard: a threefold cord is not quickly broken. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he is the third person between the two, making the relationship one. People who live for self hold on by themselves as two; people who live in selflessness let Jesus be in the middle. The third strand is the Lord.
think: What kind of cord does Eccl 4:12 say is not quickly broken?
In my relationships, where is God’s place? In the middle, or off to the side?
Whom can I invite to be a spiritual companion for our relationship?
lessons.speak: Lord, I want you to be the third strand in my relationships. Forgive us for relying only on ourselves and only on our feelings. Help each of us draw near to you, and together open ourselves to you, so that this cord is made strong in you. Strengthen us, too. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, for someone important to you, put God in the middle in prayer: say their name aloud and say, “Lord, you are between us.” Then send them a word of encouragement.
lessons.quick: For a relationship to be strong, the third strand must be God.
text: If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

lessons.title: Unless the LORD Builds the House
lessons.hear:
Xiaorong worked very hard at her relationship. She studied relationship skills, read many books, and demanded perfection of herself. But the harder she tried, the more tired she felt.

The psalm says, “Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain.” (Ps 127:1) This is not telling us to stop trying; it is a reminder that we are the builders, and God is the true architect.

When we think the success or failure of a relationship depends entirely on us, we crush ourselves and we crush the other person. Acknowledging that God is the builder is a release: I do my part, and God takes care of the rest.

The psalm goes on to say that unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain. In other words, even our most careful defenses depend on God.

Today, you can gently set down one burden that isn’t yours.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he said the Son can do nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing. The Bible is my standard: unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps us depend on God and not on our own effort. People who live for self think they are the architect; people who live in selflessness acknowledge that God is.
think: What does Ps 127:1 say happens to the builders without the LORD?
In my relationships, where am I striving desperately on my own?
Today, how can I hand the most tiring part of my relationship to God to build?
lessons.speak: God, you are the true builder. Forgive me for so often striving desperately on my own and demanding perfection from others. Help me do my part and leave the rest in your hands. Build my life and my relationships yourself. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, find the one thing in your relationship that you push hardest on and that wears you out most, and admit to God, “I can’t do this; please build.” Then choose to make one less over-the-top effort today.
lessons.quick: I do my part, and God is the true builder.
text: Unless the LORD builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless the LORD watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.

lessons.title: Through Wisdom a House Is Built
lessons.hear:
Jie believed that as long as there was a spark, nothing else mattered. Only when he found that the two of them were far apart on money, time, and values did he realize that feelings are not enough.

Proverbs says, “Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established.” (Prov 24:3) Wisdom is the ability to apply God’s word to real life; understanding is seeing the facts clearly in reality.

This means that preparing for a lasting relationship takes more than affection; it also takes a plan: talk honestly about each other’s values, views on finances, family backgrounds, and thoughts about the future, and ask experienced people to look at it with you.

This is not calculating; it is learning to love with wisdom. Feelings are the fire, and wisdom is the fireplace; with a fireplace, the fire can warm the whole house instead of burning it down.

Loving with wisdom is also a way of honoring God and honoring people.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and people. The Bible is my standard: through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives wisdom to those who sincerely ask. People who live for self act on impulse from their feelings; people who live in selflessness depend on God’s wisdom and are humble enough to be taught.
think: What does Prov 24:3 say a house is built by, and established by?
In my relationships, do I look only at feelings and avoid talking about real-life issues?
With whom can I start a wise conversation today?
lessons.speak: Lord, I need your wisdom. Help me not to go only by feelings but to see reality clearly; not to avoid difficult topics, and not to speak in a cold way. Give me wisdom and understanding, so that what I build is established in you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, list three topics you want to talk about honestly in your relationship (values, money, family, or the future). Choose one, and ask a trusted elder or companion how to begin the conversation.
lessons.quick: Feelings are the fire and wisdom is the fireplace; you need both.
text: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
by knowledge the rooms are filled with all rare and beautiful treasure.

lessons.title: As for Me and My House
lessons.hear:
Look back on this week: looking to Jesus together (Heb 12:2); letting God be the third strand (Eccl 4:12); acknowledging that God is the builder (Ps 127:1); building with wisdom (Prov 24:3).

When Joshua was old, he said to the people, “as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.” (Josh 24:15) He did not decide for anyone else; he simply declared his own choice clearly.

Whether you are single, dating, or preparing for marriage, you can make the same declaration today: my life, and the relationships I belong to, I will use to serve the LORD.

This is not a demand on others; it starts with yourself: first take your own stand, and then invite others to walk with you. Ask yourself: Where did I see my self-centeredness this week? How did God hold me up in the middle of it?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he served only the Father his whole life. The Bible is my standard; I choose to serve the LORD. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he helps me live out this choice. The order of relationships: first God, then self, others, and things. Let Jesus be King, and give all the glory to God.
think: What declaration did Joshua make in Josh 24:15?
Where did I see my self-centeredness this week? How did God hold me up in the middle of it?
In one sentence, what is the choice I want to declare to God?
lessons.speak: LORD my God, today I declare: as for me and my house, I will serve you. Forgive me for so often putting other things before you. Help me live out this choice. All glory to you. Give me perseverance, too. Amen.
lessons.do: Write your declaration in your journal: “As for me and my (future) house, we will serve the LORD.” Also write down what you discovered this week and one habit you will keep.
lessons.quick: First make your own choice, then invite others to walk with you.
text: If it seems evil to you to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”

weeks.keyText: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

weeks.title: Preparing to Enter Marriage
weeks.theme: Preparing for marriage is not about finding the right person, but about becoming someone who loves like Christ.
group: Who is the standard of love in Eph 5:25? How did he love?
Which of my expectations for marriage come from God’s word, and which come from the world or my family of origin?
In what area do I want to practice self-giving love this week? Ask your group members to pray for you.
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday service, find a married older believer with a good testimony and ask: “What do you think is most important to prepare before marriage?” Write down three sentences and pray together. Then send one sentence to a friend: “Preparing for marriage means first becoming someone who knows how to love.”
weeks.weekend: This weekend, with a spiritual companion of the same gender, work through a “marriage preparation list”: my values, my views on money, my family background, and the ways I am most likely to hurt others. Don’t aim for completeness, only for honesty. At the end, pray for each other and set a time to review it together in one month.

lessons.title: Husbands, Love Your Wives
lessons.hear:
Xiaojie had always assumed that preparing for marriage meant finding the right person. Then an older believer said to him: Don’t ask yet who the right person is. First ask yourself whether you are becoming someone who knows how to love.

Paul writes: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her.” (Eph 5:25) In this sentence, the standard of love is not a feeling, and it is not the other person’s performance. It is Christ, who gave himself up for the church.

Christ’s love has several marks: it takes the initiative, it sacrifices, it seeks the other person’s good, and it does not control. This is not just a requirement for husbands. It is a love that everyone preparing for marriage should learn.

You don’t have to wait until you are married to begin learning this kind of love. Today, in your relationships with family, friends, and companions, you can practice it.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he gave himself up for the church and loved to the end. The Bible is my standard: as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he pours Christ’s love into our hearts. A person ruled by self loves in order to receive; a person living in selflessness loves for the other person’s benefit. Love is something we learn.
think: In Eph 5:25, what is the standard of love?
Right now, is my love for others more about taking or about giving?
Today, how can I practice Christ’s initiating, sacrificial love in one relationship?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for giving yourself up for me. Teach me to love as you love: taking the initiative, sacrificing, and seeking the good of the other person without controlling. Please change me first, so that I become someone who knows how to love. Please give me perseverance as well. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, choose someone near you and do one small thing without expecting anything in return: help with a chore, buy a drink, or write a thank-you note.
lessons.quick: Preparing for marriage means first learning to love the way Christ loves.
text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,

lessons.title: Live With Your Wife According to Knowledge
lessons.hear:
Ming loved his girlfriend very much, but he often did things “for her own good” in his own way: deciding for her what to eat, replying to her friends’ messages for her. He thought this was caring for her, but she felt controlled.

Peter writes that a husband should be “giving honor to the woman.” (1 Pet 3:7) To honor someone is to treat them as just as precious as you are: equally loved by God, and equally “joint heirs of the grace of life.”

The verse says “as to the weaker vessel.” This does not mean that women are inferior. It points to the fact that in that society, women were more easily harmed in physical strength and social standing, so God requires the one with power to use that power to protect and honor, not to control.

To “live according to knowledge” is to be willing to get to know the other person, to understand their needs and limits. To honor is to refuse to overpower the other person, and this is also proof of love.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he treated women and the weak with the utmost respect. The Bible is my standard: those who are joint heirs of the grace of life with you, so honor them. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps us see every person’s dignity. A person ruled by self uses power to dominate; a person living in selflessness uses power to protect.
think: According to 1 Pet 3:7, why should we honor the other person?
In my relationships, have I ever made decisions for someone else in the name of “what’s best for you”?
Today, how can I show more respect for someone’s thoughts and boundaries?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for making every person in your image. Please forgive me for controlling others in my own way. Teach me to respect, to understand the other person’s needs, and to use my strength to protect people rather than suppress them. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, in one area where you usually decide for someone else, ask them first instead: “What do you think?” Then listen carefully to the end, without interrupting.
lessons.quick: To honor someone is to refuse to overpower them.
text: You husbands, in the same way, live with your wives according to knowledge, giving honor to the woman as to the weaker vessel, as also being joint heirs of the grace of life, that your prayers may not be hindered.

lessons.title: Whoever Finds a Wife Finds a Good Thing
lessons.hear:
When Xiaoqi heard this verse, she felt very uncomfortable: “So do I have to become a good thing for someone else in order to have worth?”

Proverbs says: “Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing,” and receives favor from the Lord. (Prov 18:22) This is an observation about wise marriage. It is not a guarantee for every person, and it does not mean that women exist to provide benefits to men.

What it really means is that a marriage that fits God’s heart is a favor given by God. In the same way, a wise person who fears God is a good thing in other people’s lives.

So preparing for marriage is not about becoming a qualified “good thing.” It is about becoming a person who fears God and has character, hoping that God will lead you into a fitting relationship, while also accepting that God may have a different calling for you. Your worth does not come from other people’s needs. It comes from God’s love.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: his worth came from the Father’s love, not from people’s opinions. The Bible is my standard: favor from the Lord. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he lets me know that I am loved. A person ruled by self proves themselves by being needed; a person living in selflessness finds worth in God’s love.
think: According to Prov 18:22, whose favor does such a marriage come from?
Do I often measure my worth by whether anyone wants me?
Today, how can I remind myself that my worth is in God’s love?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for loving me. My worth is in your love. Please heal me, so that I no longer measure myself by whether anyone wants me. Make me a person who fears you, and whichever path you lead me on, I will trust you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write down three true sentences about yourself: I am loved by God; I am made by God; I am… (fill in a quality of your character). Put them by your mirror and read them three times today.
lessons.quick: My worth is in God’s love, not in whether I am needed.
text: Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favor of the LORD.

lessons.title: What God Has Joined Together, Let No One Tear Apart
lessons.hear:
While preparing for marriage, Hui heard Matt 19:6 and was frightened: “‘What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.’ Does that mean a marriage can never be left, no matter what happens?”

Jesus said: “What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.” (Matt 19:6) This was his answer to the Pharisees, who wanted to divorce their wives for careless reasons. Jesus’ point is that marriage is a serious covenant established by God and must not be casually torn down.

His words are meant to protect the more vulnerable party in a marriage. They are not meant to lock people into violence and harm. We have to hold two things together: marriage is a sacred covenant and must be taken seriously; and, at the same time, personal safety matters more than anything else.

So preparing for marriage means taking it seriously before entering it, preparing honestly, and walking with people you can trust. If there is any violence, control, or fear, please seek help first, and be sure to reach out to a professional or a pastor.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he took marriage seriously, and he had compassion for the wounded. The Bible is my standard: what God has joined together, let no one tear apart, which protects people rather than harm. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives wisdom so that we can clearly discern between covenant and safety. A person ruled by self uses Scripture to pressure people; a person living in selflessness uses Scripture to guard people.
think: What is the background of Matt 19:6? Who is asking what question?
Does my view of marriage as a covenant bring me reverence or fear?
If someone around me is being hurt in a relationship, how can I help them find safety and support?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for establishing marriage. Help me take the covenant of marriage seriously, and help me see every person’s safety and dignity. Protect those who are hurting, and give me wisdom, so that I do not use your words to hurt people but to guard them. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, spend ten minutes writing down three hopes and three worries you have about marriage, and make a time to talk honestly with a trusted older believer or counselor. If you are facing violence or control, please call Taiwan’s 113 protection hotline or 110.
lessons.quick: Marriage is a sacred covenant, and personal safety matters more than anything.
text: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”

lessons.title: Blessed Is Everyone Who Fears the Lord
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: preparing for marriage means first learning to love the way Christ loves (Eph 5:25); honoring and respecting others (1 Pet 3:7); knowing that my worth is in God’s love (Prov 18:22); and taking the marriage covenant seriously while also valuing people’s safety (Matt 19:6).

The psalm says: “Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD,” the one who walks in his ways. (Ps 128:1) The source of blessing is not a spouse, children, or wealth, but fearing the Lord.

The psalmist paints a beautiful picture of a family, but it is a blessing received by those who fear God, not a guarantee for everyone. Some people are blessed yet walk a different road; a single person can also be blessed in the fear of God.

Ask yourself: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he loved the church and gave himself up for her. The Bible is my standard; fear the Lord and walk in his ways. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he helps me live in reverence. The order of relationships: first with God, then with self, others, and things. Let Jesus be King, and give the glory to God.
think: According to Ps 128:1, who is blessed?
Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?
How can I begin, starting today, to live a life that fears the Lord?
lessons.speak: Lord my God, I will fear you and walk in your ways. Help me put you first, so that whether I am single or enter marriage in the future, I will be blessed in you. Make me a person who loves like Christ. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, write down: my biggest discovery this week; the one thing I most want to change in my lessons on love; and one habit I will keep. Then today, send a word of thanks to an older believer you want to learn from.
lessons.quick: The source of blessing is fearing the Lord.
text: Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD, who walks in his ways.
For you will eat the labor of your hands. You will be happy, and it will be well with you.
Your wife will be as a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house, your children like olive shoots around your table.
Behold, this is how the man who fears the LORD is blessed.

weeks.keyText: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,

weeks.title: Letting Go Honestly: Ending a Relationship Well
weeks.theme: An ending can also be honest and gracious; if there is danger, you are allowed to leave, and it is not your fault.
group: What “times” does Eccl 3:5–6 list? In my experience, which time is the hardest?
How have I ended (or been left in) a relationship? What did I need most at that time?
This week, how can I walk beside someone who has just ended a relationship, without giving advice and without criticizing?
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday service, find a companion you trust and take two minutes to say: “What I need to let go of is…” The other person only listens, and prays for you for three minutes. If you or someone around you is in a relationship marked by threats or control, please tell a trusted pastor or counselor today, and call Taiwan’s 113 protection hotline.
weeks.weekend: This weekend, set up a “ritual of letting go.” With a companion, in a quiet place, write down three things you need to hand over to God (a loss, a resentment, a worry). Pray over each one, then put the paper in an envelope, write the date on it, and ask your companion to keep it for you. Afterward, share a meal together to celebrate that you faced things honestly.

lessons.title: A Time to Cast Away, a Time to Embrace, a Time to Seek, a Time to Lose
lessons.hear:
After Xiaoyu broke up with the boyfriend she had dated for two years, an older believer told her: “Pray more, and God will bring you back together.” So she waited a year, only to find that he had never changed, and that she herself had lost much of her peace.

Ecclesiastes says there is “a time to seek,” and also a time to lose, a time to keep, and a time to cast away. (Eccl 3:6) These words admit that life holds loss and letting go; ending a relationship is not necessarily a failure.

Sometimes an ending comes because two people are headed in different directions; sometimes because one person has not truly repented; sometimes because there is harm and danger there.

Please remember: being hurt is not your fault. If there is control, threats, violence, or fear, you are allowed to leave, and God protects you in doing so. If you or someone around you is in danger, please seek help first: 113, 110, or a pastor or counselor you trust. Safety always comes before everything else.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he has compassion for the wounded and protects the victimized. The Bible is my standard: a time to keep and a time to cast away. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives wisdom so that I know when to let go. A person ruled by self clings to the death, or refuses to let go for the sake of face; a person living in selflessness is honest before God and willing to let go.
think: According to Eccl 3:6, which two “times” come as a pair?
Have I ever stayed in an unhealthy relationship because of fear, guilt, or other people’s expectations?
Who can I tell the truth to today, and ask for help?
lessons.speak: God, thank you for knowing all my losses. Help me keep what should be kept and let go of what should be let go. Protect those who are hurt, give courage to those who need to leave, and let us have peace in your grace. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, save the phone numbers of two people you trust in the most easily reached place on your phone. If you are in an unsafe relationship, contact one of them right now, or call Taiwan’s 113 protection hotline.
lessons.quick: An ending is not necessarily a failure; leaving danger is allowed.
text: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

lessons.title: Do Not Let a Root of Bitterness Spring Up
lessons.hear:
After being broken up with, Xiang stopped reaching out to anyone. Every day he replayed what the other person had said, getting angrier the more he thought about it, and more and more convinced that nobody could be trusted. A year later, he found that he had become cold and distant.

Hebrews warns, “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you.” (Heb 12:15) Bitterness is like a root: at first it is hardly noticeable, but slowly it grows branches and leaves, hurting you and the people around you.

The root of bitterness often begins with a wound that was never dealt with. Admitting your anger, sadness, and sense of grievance, and bringing them to God, is the first step in pulling out the root.

Be clear about this: forgiveness is something you can give first, because it is how you lay down a burden; trust, however, has to be rebuilt slowly through the other person’s genuine repentance and actions. Forgiveness does not mean going back to the other person, and it does not mean having no boundaries.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: on the cross he said, Father, forgive them. The Bible is my standard: do not let a root of bitterness spring up. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he heals our wounds and leads us out of bitterness. A person ruled by self holds on to the hurt and becomes their own judge; a person living in selflessness hands the hurt to God, the righteous judge.
think: According to Heb 12:15, what are the consequences when a root of bitterness springs up?
Is there a wound or resentment in my heart that has not yet been dealt with?
Today, how can I bring one wound to God?
lessons.speak: Lord, I am wounded, and I carry resentment. Please heal me, and do not let a root of bitterness grow in my heart. Help me face things honestly, and give me strength to hand all this over to you. Teach me to forgive, and protect me from being hurt again. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write a letter you will not send. Honestly write down what you want to say to the other person, including your anger and sadness. When you finish, pray to God, and then tear the letter up or put it away.
lessons.quick: Give your wound to God to deal with; do not let it turn into bitterness.
text: looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it,

lessons.title: Repay No One Evil for Evil
lessons.hear:
After the breakup, Xin badly wanted the other person to know how deeply she had been hurt. She posted hints on social media and told mutual friends what he had done wrong. At first it felt satisfying, but later she felt even emptier.

Paul writes: “Repay no one evil for evil.” (Rom 12:17) Revenge, whether public or hidden, will not make your wound any better.

Then he says: “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.” (Rom 12:18) Notice “if it is possible”: it admits that sometimes it is not. Peace takes two people, and if the other person is dangerous or unrepentant, you do not have to, and should not, go back into that relationship for the sake of peace.

What you can do is not harm the other person, not spread gossip, and not pay back an eye for an eye, while protecting yourself with boundaries. This is both honest and wise.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: when he was insulted he did not answer back, and he entrusted himself to the righteous judge. The Bible is my standard: repay no one evil for evil. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives us self-control, and he gives us boundaries. A person ruled by self demands justice; a person living in selflessness leaves justice to God and keeps the boundaries for themselves.
think: In Rom 12:18, what do the words “if it is possible” remind me of?
Since the breakup, have I used words or actions to try to hurt the other person?
Today, how can I avoid revenge and still protect myself?
lessons.speak: Lord, I have been hurt, and I badly want the other person to feel the pain too. Please forgive my desire for revenge. Give me self-control, so that I do not repay evil for evil, and give me wisdom to set boundaries that protect me. I leave justice with you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, check your social media and messages: is there anything you want to send or post out of revenge? Save it as a draft first and look at it again after twenty-four hours. If needed, mute or block the other person’s contact to protect yourself.
lessons.quick: Do not take revenge, and do not force yourself back into danger.
text: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.

lessons.title: You Have Turned My Mourning into Dancing
lessons.hear:
For three months after the breakup, Xuan wanted to cry every morning when she woke up. She worried that she was not spiritual enough, because others said that believers should always be joyful.

The psalmist says: “You have turned my mourning into dancing for me.” (Ps 30:11) The premise of this line is that he mourned first. God does not ask us to skip over mourning. He is with us in the midst of it, and in his time he makes joy new in us again.

So mourning is allowed. You can be sad, you can miss them, you can be angry; these are all evidence that you loved. What matters is that you do not cry alone, and that you do not stay stuck there.

Please find someone who can be with you, and pay attention to your body: sleep, eating, and exercise. If the grief lasts a long time, affects your daily life, or you begin to have thoughts of harming yourself, please see a counselor or a doctor right away, and you can also call Taiwan’s 1925 mental-health hotline.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he wept at Lazarus’s tomb, and he wept with those who weep. The Bible is my standard: you have turned my mourning into dancing. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he is the Comforter, who comforts us. A person ruled by self suppresses or rejects emotions; a person living in selflessness faces them honestly and lets God comfort them.
think: According to Ps 30:11, what did God turn into what?
Have I ever refused to let myself grieve properly because of other people’s expectations?
Today, in what way can I allow myself to grieve quietly?
lessons.speak: Jesus, thank you for weeping for your friend too. Please keep company with my sorrow, so that I do not suppress it or carry it alone. In your time, turn my mourning into dancing. And make me willing to open up to someone I trust. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, give yourself one hour: take a walk, take a hot bath, listen to a worship song, and let yourself feel sad naturally. Afterward, send a message to someone you trust: “I’ve been having a hard time lately. Can you spend some time talking with me?”
lessons.quick: Mourning is allowed; God will keep you company, and he will renew you.
text: You have turned my mourning into dancing for me. You have removed my sackcloth, and clothed me with gladness,

lessons.title: Cast Everything on Him, and Stop Entangling Yourself
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: there is a time to end (Eccl 3:6); do not let a root of bitterness spring up (Heb 12:15); do not repay evil for evil, and set boundaries (Rom 12:17–18); mourning is allowed, and God comforts (Ps 30:11).

The psalm says: “Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you.” (Ps 55:22) To cast it is to truly set it down, not to pick it up again every day.

Some people say with their mouths that they have let go, while in their hearts they keep going over old accounts, checking the other person’s updates, or replaying conversations in their heads. This is entanglement, not entrusting. Entrusting takes a deliberate choice, and it takes the company of others.

If you are ending a relationship, do not rush into the next one; first let God heal you. Ask yourself: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he entrusted everything to the Father. The Bible is my standard; cast your burden on the LORD. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he helps me let go. The order of relationships: first with God, then with self, others, and things. Let Jesus be King, and give the glory to God.
think: According to Ps 55:22, what will God do for me after I cast my burden on him?
Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week (entanglement, tracking, revenge, suppression)? How did God sustain me in it?
What is the one thing I will deliberately let go of? Who can I ask to walk with me in it?
lessons.speak: Lord my God, I cast my burden on you. Sustain me, so that I no longer entangle myself, track the other person, or go over old accounts. Heal my heart, and protect me. I will stand up again in your grace. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, write down: my biggest discovery this week; the one thing I will let go of today; and the people and phone numbers I can turn to for help. Then today, delete or hide one update, photo, or conversation that keeps entangling you.
lessons.quick: Entrusting is deliberately setting it down, not picking it up again.
text: Cast your burden on the LORD and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.

weeks.keyText: a time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

weeks.title: Spiritual Companions
weeks.theme: Let trustworthy people know your real situation, and walk beside others on this road.
group: Which generations of entrusting does 2 Tim 2:2 mention? What is the requirement for the people entrusted?
Do you have a companion right now you can tell the truth to? If not, what makes it hard to open up?
This week, who are you willing to share a little more of your real self with, or to walk beside? Ask your group members to pray for you.
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday service, find a brother or sister you trust, and take three minutes to say to each other: “The one thing I most need prayer for this week is…” Then pray for each other. Then send one thing you heard today to a friend.
weeks.weekend: This weekend, invite a spiritual companion (or two or three friends) for a cup of tea. Each of you shares one real situation from this month, without giving advice, only listening and praying. Before you finish, set a time for your next meeting.

lessons.title: Entrust to Faithful People
lessons.hear:
Xiaojie had served for many years, and everyone said he was an example, yet nobody knew the struggle in his heart. He asked himself how he could possibly let people see his weakness. An older believer asked him whether he had anyone he could tell the truth to. He was silent for a long time.

Paul tells Timothy: “The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” (2 Tim 2:2) This verse has four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful people, and others. Life is not kept for ourselves; it is handed down from one generation to the next.

The ones entrusted are the “faithful,” not the most capable. In a spiritual companion, what matters is who is reliable, who will tell the truth, and who is willing to walk with you. On the road of dating, we need people like this, who will help us see clearly when we cannot.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he entrusted his life to twelve disciples and walked with them for three years. The Bible is my standard: entrust what you have heard to faithful people who can teach others. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he prepares trustworthy companions for us. A person ruled by self tries to hold on alone; a person living in selflessness is willing to be accompanied, and to accompany others. Everyone I am in relationship with is my 2, and this is how companionship begins.
think: In 2 Tim 2:2, to what kind of people does Paul tell Timothy to entrust what he has heard?
Am I used to carrying everything alone, not letting anyone see the real me?
Who around me is faithful and reliable, someone I could draw a little closer to?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for not letting me walk this road alone. Give me faithful, reliable companions, and make me someone others can rely on. Take away my pride, so that I dare to let people see the real me, and am willing to pass on what I have received from you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, take the initiative to send a message to a companion you trust: “Lately I’ve wanted to find some time to talk with you. Are you free?” Just ask for a time; you don’t need to say much first.
lessons.quick: A spiritual companion is not the most impressive person, but the one who is faithful, reliable, and willing to tell the truth.
text: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.

lessons.title: Glad to Share the Good News of God and Our Own Lives
lessons.hear:
The week Xiaoya broke up, a sister sent her one line every day: I’m here, and there’s no rush to talk. She did not give answers, and she did not say, “It’s time to let go.” She simply ate with Xiaoya, cried with her, and prayed with her. Xiaoya said later that it was the first time she felt that the gospel has warmth.

Paul describes his relationship with the Thessalonians this way: “not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls.” (1 Thess 2:8) He gave both the gospel and his life. Doctrine without companionship is like talking through glass; companionship without truth easily becomes people just keeping each other warm.

Note that accompanying is service, not control. A companion can remind, pray, and think things through together, but does not decide for the other person whether to date or whether to break up.

A companion’s presence does not need to be perfect, only consistent.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he became flesh and dwelt among us, and gave us both the gospel and his own life. The Bible is my standard: give the gospel and life together. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives us strength to accompany people. Accompanying with self wants to control the outcome; accompanying in selflessness simply is there, and points to Jesus.
think: In 1 Thess 2:8, what else did Paul give them besides the gospel?
When I accompanied others in the past, did I rush to give answers or make decisions for them?
Today, how can I simply keep one person company?
lessons.speak: Jesus, you gave me both the gospel and your own life. Make me willing to accompany others too, without rushing to preach and without wanting to control. Help me come close to people with your gentleness and truth, so that people see you in me. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, choose a friend who is having a hard time and call or message them: “I’m here. You can talk whenever you need.” Give no advice; just keep them company for ten minutes.
lessons.quick: Give the gospel and life together; accompanying is not controlling, it is simply being there.
text: Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.

lessons.title: Timothy, Who Truly Cares About You
lessons.hear:
Paul was in prison, yet he was still concerned for others. He says: “I have no one else like-minded, who will truly care about you.” (Phil 2:20) The person he had in mind was Timothy.

Paul goes on to say that they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ (Phil 2:21). This is a sobering line: in any group, few people truly care about others.

Timothy’s distinguishing trait was not eloquence or talent, but “truly caring.” This is exactly what selflessness looks like: not first thinking about what I can get, but first thinking about what the other person needs.

In dating and in friendship, we can also ask ourselves: Do I truly care about this person’s life, or do I only want comfort and satisfaction from this relationship? The latter is not bad, but it is not enough.

Timothy’s example is worth learning together.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he cares about every sheep, even going to find the one that is lost. The Bible is my standard: truly care about others, and do not seek only your own. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he puts a love that cares for people into our hearts. A person ruled by self first asks, “What do I get?”; a person living in selflessness first asks, “What does he need?”
think: According to Phil 2:20, how was Timothy different from the others around Paul?
In relationships, do I more often think about what I get, or about what the other person needs?
Who can I truly care about and pray for today?
lessons.speak: Lord, give me a heart like Timothy’s, one that truly cares about others and does not seek only my own. Forgive me for so often being self-centered. Help me, in every relationship, to see people’s needs first, and to learn to pray for them. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, pray for three people for one minute each. Write down their names, and send a message to one of them: “I prayed for you today.”
lessons.quick: A person living in selflessness first cares about the other’s life, rather than first thinking about what they get.
text: But I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered up when I know how you are doing.
For I have no one else like-minded, who will truly care about you.
For they all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.
But you know that he has proved himself. As a child serves a father, so he served with me in furtherance of the Good News.

lessons.title: Walk With the Wise
lessons.hear:
En said that the circle he had recently been spending time with was lively, with frequent meals together and fun, but every time he went home, his heart felt empty, and his devotional time had stopped. A friend asked him: Does this group bring you closer to God, or farther away?

Proverbs says: “One who walks with wise men grows wise,” but a companion of fools suffers harm. (Prov 13:20) The people we walk with quietly change us.

This verse does not tell us to label people or to judge others as fools, and it does not teach us to cut off all our friends. It asks us to check honestly: Where is the circle around me taking me?

Dating is also a kind of walking together. The person closest to you will influence your faith, values, and habits. Find people to walk with who are like the person you want to become; and at the same time, become someone others can walk with in confidence.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he drew near to sinners without being carried away by them, because he walked with the Father. The Bible is my standard: one who walks with the wise grows wise. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps us see the influence our circle has on us. A person ruled by self picks friends by feeling; a person living in selflessness lets God’s wisdom guide the choice.
think: According to Prov 13:20, what does someone who walks with the wise gain?
Does the circle around me bring me closer to God, or farther away?
Which person could I draw closer to, or in what setting could I put a little distance?
lessons.speak: Lord, give me wisdom to see who is influencing me. Let me walk with people who fear you, and make me a blessing to others. Heal my loneliness, so that I do not leave you just to fit in. And heal me, so that I am no longer lonely. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write down on paper the five people you spend the most time with, and next to each write: How does this person affect my relationship with God? Then choose one and invite him to read the Bible or pray together this week.
lessons.quick: Who we walk with quietly changes us; choose your companions on purpose.
text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.

lessons.title: Exhort One Another Day by Day
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: spiritual companions must be faithful (2 Tim 2:2); companions give the gospel and life (1 Thess 2:8); truly care about others (Phil 2:20); walk with the wise (Prov 13:20).

Hebrews says: “exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called ‘today’, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” (Heb 3:13) The deceitfulness of sin often comes quietly, a little at a time, until the heart grows hard. To exhort one another is to have someone pull us back before we are deceived.

Exhorting is not judging, and it is not controlling. Good exhortation has three things: it carries love, it carries truth, and it stays within what the other person is willing to receive.

This week, you may have found that you are not used to being exhorted, or that you do not quite dare to exhort others. Ask yourself: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he gave his life for us. The Bible is my standard; exhort one another day by day. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he keeps our hearts soft so that we are not deceived by sin. Only selflessness can be exhorted, and only selflessness can bring unity. The 2 in the 2-3-5 is spiritual companions who are willing to exhort one another.
think: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week?
According to Heb 3:13, what is the purpose of exhorting one another?
How did God sustain me in it this week? Who can I open up to?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for sustaining me this week. Soften my heart, so that I am willing to be reminded by a companion, and give me courage to speak honestly in love. Keep me from being deceived by sin, so that we exhort one another and walk this road to the end together. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, write down: where my self-centeredness showed up this week; how God sustained me; and who I want to invite to exhort one another. Today, send them a word and agree on a weekly check-in.
lessons.quick: To exhort one another is to have someone pull us back before we are deceived by sin.
text: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

weeks.keyText: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.

weeks.title: Spiritual Parents and Spiritual Children
weeks.theme: A life of love can be passed on; we can also become companions to young people.
group: According to 1 Cor 4:15, what is the difference between a father and a tutor?
Do I have spiritual parents or children in my life? Does that relationship bring me closer to Jesus, or make me more dependent on people?
This week, who am I willing to ask for advice, or to share what I have received with? Ask your group members to pray for you.
weeks.sunday: After the service, say to a brother or sister older than you: “I’d like to ask you a question.” If you are the older one, say to a younger person: “Is there anything I can pray with you about lately?” And send one sentence from today to a friend.
weeks.weekend: This weekend, invite a believer older than you to a meal and ask three questions: how he met Jesus, what low points he has been through, and how God brought him through. You only listen, and pray for him.

lessons.title: In Christ Jesus I Became Your Father Through the Gospel
lessons.hear:
At church, Xiaofen met an older sister who always took time to listen to her and often prayed with her. One day Xiaofen said that she was like a spiritual mother to her. The sister smiled and said that we are all children being raised by God.

Paul tells the Corinthians: “Though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.” (1 Cor 4:15) A tutor teaches knowledge, but a parent gives life. There are many who teach, but few who are willing to give their lives and walk beside someone over the long term.

Spiritual parents are not controllers, and they are not idols. Their role is to bring you to Jesus, and in the end to let you grow up and walk with the Lord on your own.

You can also ask yourself: Who brought me to Jesus like this? And whom can I bring to Jesus? The answer need not be big; starting with one person is enough.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he personally taught and accompanied his disciples, and in the end sent them out. The Bible is my standard: one who gives birth to others through the gospel in Christ Jesus is like a father. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he passes spiritual life on from one generation to the next. Spiritual parents ruled by self want others to depend on them; spiritual parents living in selflessness bring people to Jesus. The 3 is the relationship between spiritual parents and children.
think: In 1 Cor 4:15, why does Paul call himself a “father”?
Is there someone in my life who has accompanied me like a spiritual parent?
Can I also become a spiritual older brother, sister, or parent to someone else?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for using people to bring the gospel to me. Give me spiritual parents and companions, and make me willing to hand the life I have received to the next generation. Protect all who lead, so that they do not control or become proud, but only bring people to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write a thank-you card to someone who has helped you in your faith, with one specific word of thanks: what he did that brought you closer to God.
lessons.quick: Spiritual parents bring people to Jesus, and in the end let them walk with the Lord on their own.
text: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.
I beg you therefore, be imitators of me.

lessons.title: The Sincere Faith in You
lessons.hear:
Mei grew up to the sound of her grandmother’s prayers. As a child she found it annoying, but when she went through a low point as an adult, she discovered that the hymns and prayers were still in her heart. She said that it was the greatest inheritance her grandmother left her.

Paul writes to Timothy: “Having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.” (2 Tim 1:5) Faith is like a lamp passed from one generation to the next, not through heredity, but through the testimony of daily life.

If you come from a family without faith, don’t be discouraged: you can be the first lamp in your family. If your family has hurt you, this verse is not asking you to treat the hurt as an inheritance; it is a reminder that God can begin a new spiritual generation.

May we all become people who pass faith on.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he lived out the Father’s love and moved many generations. The Bible is my standard: sincere faith is passed from the heart to the next generation. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he makes our faith genuine, not false. A faith ruled by self is a performance; a faith living in selflessness is real life.
think: According to 2 Tim 1:5, where did Timothy’s faith come from?
Is my faith genuine, or is part of it only habit or performance?
Whose lamp do I want to be? What can I do today?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for passing faith on to me through the prayers and testimony of so many people. Make my faith genuine and sincere, and let it be a light to others. If my family bears wounds, please heal them, and make me a new beginning. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, pray for someone who has prayed for you or given you a testimony, and send them a message: “Thank you. Your faith has influenced me.” If there is no such person, pray for the people you will one day influence.
lessons.quick: Faith is like a lamp, passed from one generation to the next through genuine daily life.
text: having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.

lessons.title: Teaching the Young Women
lessons.hear:
Lian had only recently come to faith, and an older sister often invited her for tea, teaching her how to read the Bible and how to handle her emotions. Once Lian said that she was very afraid her future partner would not respect her. After listening, the sister first prayed for her, and then shared her own experience, without giving any list of people and without giving Lian any conditions.

Paul tells Titus to urge the older women to be “teachers of that which is good, that they may train the young wives.” (Titus 2:3–5) This passage has three points: the older must be examples; the way of teaching is what is good; and the purpose is that God’s word may not be blasphemed.

Pay special attention: the family roles mentioned in this passage are never a demand that anyone stay in violence, control, or harm. If someone is being hurt, personal safety comes first, and only then the rest.

May we learn to speak with grace.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he taught people with parables and with life, and did not shame them. The Bible is my standard: teach what is good, so that God’s word is not blasphemed. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives the older wisdom and the younger a willingness to learn. Teaching ruled by self carries comparison and criticism; teaching living in selflessness carries example and grace.
think: According to Titus 2:3–5, in what way should older people teach younger people?
Have I received “teaching” that carried criticism or comparison? What effect did it have on me?
Which older brother or sister can I ask for advice, and on what life issue?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for using older believers to teach us. Let those who teach do so with what is good, carrying love, and let those who are taught receive it humbly. Protect the wounded, and let truth and grace come to them together. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, ask an older believer a specific question, for example: “How did you learn to speak honestly in relationships?” And write down in pen the most helpful sentence.
lessons.quick: Good teaching carries example and grace, not criticism and comparison.
text: and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good,
that they may train the young wives to love their husbands, to love their children,
to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.

lessons.title: Urging the Young to Be Sober Minded
lessons.hear:
Xiaoyu is in his twenties and leads a youth fellowship. He once told himself that he was still learning in his own marriage and relationships, so how could he dare to teach anyone else? A pastor answered him: You don’t need to be perfect; you need to be genuine, and to walk with God.

Paul instructs Titus: “Exhort the younger men to be sober minded. In all things show yourself an example of good works.” (Titus 2:6–7) To be an example does not mean having no weakness, but being honest, humble, and obedient to God in the midst of weakness.

Example often influences people more deeply than preaching. What young people want to see is not how much you say, but how you live: how you treat the opposite sex, how you handle money, and how you return to God after failing.

You may not be married yet, and you may still be healing, but God can still use your genuineness to help others.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he not only spoke but lived it out; his words and actions were completely consistent. The Bible is my standard: in all things be an example of good works, with integrity, seriousness, and sound speech. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he keeps us honest even in our weakness. An example ruled by self wants to be praised; an example living in selflessness only wants people to see Jesus.
think: According to Titus 2:7, what kind of example do the young need to see?
In what area of my life might I be influencing the young people around me?
In which weakness can I honestly show others how to return to God?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, make me an example to others in word and in conduct. I am not perfect; make me honest, humble in repenting when I fall, and not covering things up. Let my life help people see you more clearly. And make me the same before people and in private. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, examine one habit in your life (for example, how you text or the words you use), and choose one adjustment to make it more like Jesus. Write it down and tell a companion.
lessons.quick: An example is not someone without weakness, but someone who is honest and humble in weakness and returns to God.
text: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded.
In all things show yourself an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,
and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.

lessons.title: Be an Example to the Believers
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: spiritual parents bring people to Jesus (1 Cor 4:15); faith is passed down through the generations (2 Tim 1:5); teaching with what is good (Titus 2:3–5); an example of good works (Titus 2:7).

Paul says to Timothy: “Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.” (1 Tim 4:12) Youth is not an excuse, and it is not a defect; God can use people of any age. Five areas, speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity, are also five checkpoints for your dating life.

This week, you may have seen where you need to be led, and also where you can lead others. Ask yourself: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he is the example for people, and for us. The Bible is my standard; be an example to the believers. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he gives us the strength to live it out. Only selflessness can become a spiritual parent or a spiritual child; the 3 is a relationship built up together in love.
think: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week?
Which five areas does 1 Tim 4:12 list? Which one do I most need to grow in?
How did God sustain me in it this week? Who am I willing to be led by?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for this week’s teaching. Make me an example to others in speech, conduct, love, faith, and purity. Make me willing to be led, and willing to lead others. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, give each of the five areas (speech, conduct, love, faith, purity) a score from 1 to 5, choose the lowest one, and make one small change in it today.
lessons.quick: Youth is not an excuse; God uses those who are willing to be an example.
text: Let no man despise your youth; but be an example to those who believe, in word, in your way of life, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.

weeks.keyText: For though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers. For in Christ Jesus, I became your father through the Good News.

weeks.title: Leading the Next Generation in Talking About Love
weeks.theme: Walk beside the next generation, with a real life and honest conversation, as they come to know God’s love.
group: According to Deut 6:6–7, at what times can we talk about God’s word?
How was I taught about love and relationships when I was young? What is there to be thankful for, or in need of healing?
This week, on what occasion can I talk naturally about love and relationships with a young person (or a child)?
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday service, spend ten minutes chatting with a parent, a youth worker, or a young person: “What do you think young people most need to hear about love today?” And send one sentence from today to a friend.
weeks.weekend: This weekend, find a young friend (or your own child, or a younger relative) and go for a walk or have a meal together. Don’t preach; start by asking: “What are the hardest things young people run into when they date these days?” Just listen, and pray for him.

lessons.title: Teach Them Diligently to Your Children
lessons.hear:
Yong is the father of two children. When his daughter was in junior high, she suddenly asked him one day: “Dad, how did you and Mom get together?” He froze, and almost brushed it off with “kids shouldn’t ask.” In the end he sat down and told her his story, including the failures, and including God.

Moses says: “These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart; and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.” (Deut 6:6–7)

It does not say to find one class to cover it. It says to talk in the course of ordinary life: sitting, walking, at bedtime, on rising. Talking about love and relationships is the same; it needs to be natural, ongoing, and honest, not finished in one conversation.

If you have no children, you still have younger relatives, students, or young people at church, and this verse speaks to you as well.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he taught his disciples anywhere and anytime, on the road, at the table, in the boat. The Bible is my standard: keep God’s words on your heart and talk about them in daily life. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps us know when to speak and when to listen. Teaching ruled by self lectures; teaching living in selflessness lives life together.
think: According to Deut 6:6–7, at what times should we talk about God’s word?
Have I avoided talking with the next generation about love and relationships? What is the reason?
In what everyday setting can I naturally start a conversation today?
