lessons.speak: Lord, first write your words on my heart, so that I am changed by you first. Give me wisdom and courage to talk naturally with the next generation about love and relationships in daily life, without avoiding it and without preaching. And help me listen first and speak afterward. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, find a chance to talk with a young person and ask an open question: “Is there anything lately that you’d like to talk with someone about?” Just listen, without commenting or rushing to give answers.
lessons.quick: Talking about love and relationships is not one class, but natural conversation in daily life.
text: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.

lessons.title: We Will Tell the Glory of the Lord to the Next Generation
lessons.hear:
At one gathering, Xiaolei said that what moved her most was not the speaker’s eloquence, but an old brother who talked about how God had led him all his life, his eyes growing red. She said: So this is how faith can be passed on.

The psalmist says: “We will not hide them from their children,” but will tell the next generation the Lord’s excellence and might, and his wonderful works. (Ps 78:4)

Two things are to be told to the next generation: God’s excellence, and also his wonderful works. We often pass on only the rules (you may not…), and forget to pass on who God is and what God has done.

If teaching about love is left with nothing but prohibitions, young people will feel that faith is a pile of restrictions; if we first tell how God loved us and led us, the rules have roots and warmth.

This is the testimony the next generation needs most.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he revealed the Father’s love to his disciples. The Bible is my standard: tell the next generation of God’s excellence and works. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he turns testimony into living words. Handing down with self insists on my own version; handing down in selflessness tells what God has done. Let the next generation also see that faith is alive.
think: What two things does Ps 78:4 ask us to tell?
When I speak to the next generation, is it more about rules, or more about God’s love and works?
What testimony of God’s leading in my life can I tell others?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for the wonderful things you have done in my life. Help me not to hide your excellence, and not to hide your power. Help me tell of your works, so that the next generation will know you, love you, and trust you. And let my life become a testimony. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write a testimony of no more than a hundred words: how God has led me in my love life or relationships. Find a chance to tell it to a young person, or save it in your journal.
lessons.quick: First tell of God’s excellence and works, and the rules will have roots and warmth.
text: We will not hide them from their children, telling to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, his strength, and his wondrous deeds that he has done.

lessons.title: Train Up a Child in the Way He Should Go
lessons.hear:
At a family gathering, De said: “In our family we have a house rule: no boyfriends or girlfriends.” As a result, his son got a girlfriend in high school but didn’t dare tell him, and had to see her in secret. Later, when the relationship ran into trouble, his son didn’t dare ask for help, and walked alone for a long time.

Proverbs says: “Train up a child in the way he should go,” and even when he is old he will not turn away from it. (Prov 22:6) This is a principle of wisdom: good training leaves an influence; it is not a guarantee that holds for every child. Children make their own choices too, and God is the final Lord.

Training is not controlling. “The way he should go” means guiding him, according to his temperament and age, to know God, love God, and also learn to love others.

The best training is to let a child know that whatever happens, they can come back to you.

May we become safe people.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he let the children come to him, and he respected every person’s freedom. The Bible is my standard: train up a child in the way he should go. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he can do what we cannot. Training ruled by self wants to control the outcome; training living in selflessness does its part and leaves the outcome to God.
think: According to Prov 22:6, what is the aim of training?
How do I see the difference between “training” and “controlling”?
How can I let the young people around me know they can safely open up to me?
lessons.speak: Father, give me wisdom to raise those you have entrusted to me. Keep me from using control in place of love, or threats in place of guidance. Let them know that whatever happens, there is a place they can safely come back to. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, say one accepting sentence to a younger person: “Whatever happens, you can come to me, and I won’t scold you.” If there is no suitable person, pray for such a relationship.
lessons.quick: Good training lets a person know that whatever happens, they can safely come back.
text: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.

lessons.title: Turn the Hearts of the Fathers to the Children
lessons.hear:
Xiaozhi and his father had hardly talked properly for ten years. He said: Dad doesn’t understand my love life and only criticizes. He also said: I have never asked Dad how his marriage got through. One day he finally spoke up, and the two sat in the car in silence for a long time, until his father said: Actually, I was afraid you would get hurt too.

Malachi says that God will send Elijah, and “He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers.” (Mal 4:6) The reconciliation of parents and children is God’s own work.

This verse is not asking everyone to reconcile with their family immediately. If there is violence, abuse, or ongoing harm in your family, please protect yourself first and seek counseling; reconciliation needs safety, repentance, and time.

If it is possible, begin with one sincere word.

May you also have the courage to take the first small step.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he brings us back into the Father’s arms and makes us children of God. The Bible is my standard: the hearts of the fathers turned to the children, and the hearts of the children to their fathers. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives broken relationships a chance to be healed. Only selflessness can set pride down and speak first to mend things.
think: According to Mal 4:6, what will God turn to what?
Is there a word I have not said to my parents (or to a younger person)?
What is the first small step I can take, within a safe range?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for being our Father. Turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents, and heal our families. Give me wisdom and safety, so that I know when to speak, and protect those who are hurting. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, pray for five minutes about your relationship with your family, write down one sentence you want to say to them, and decide whether to say it. If there are safety concerns, please talk first with a pastor or counselor you trust.
lessons.quick: Reconciliation in a family is God’s work; safety comes first, and then reconciliation.
text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children and the hearts of the children to their fathers, lest I come and strike the earth with a curse.”

lessons.title: Encouraged Together by Each Other’s Faith
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: talking with the next generation in daily life (Deut 6:6–7); telling of God’s works (Ps 78:4); training with wisdom (Prov 22:6); fathers and children reconciled (Mal 4:6).

Paul says to the believers in Rome: “that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.” (Rom 1:12) Notice that this is mutual: though Paul is an apostle, he also needs to be encouraged by the faith of younger believers.

Those who lead the next generation also need their help. Sometimes the sincerity of young people reminds us of the first love we have forgotten. So teaching and being taught go both ways.

Ask yourself: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week? How did God sustain me in it?

So this week, whether old or young, we are members who need one another, growing up together in Christ.
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example; he walked with his disciples. The Bible is my standard; tell the next generation of God’s word and works. The Holy Spirit is my guide; he strengthens old and young together. Generations ruled by self compare and criticize one another; generations living in selflessness build one another up. This is part of building God’s system.
think: Where did I see my own self-centeredness this week?
According to Rom 1:12, what did the mutual faith of Paul and the believers bring?
How did God sustain me in it this week? What do I want to learn from a young person?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for letting old and young support one another. Make me willing not only to teach but to be taught, not only to give but to receive. Let our faith in one another bring encouragement and strength. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, write down: where my self-centeredness showed up this week; how God sustained me; and one thing I want to learn from a young person. Today, tell him: “I’d like to learn this from you.”
lessons.quick: Those who lead are also led; mutual faith lets us be encouraged together.
text: For I long to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift, to the end that you may be established;
that is, that I with you may be encouraged in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

weeks.keyText: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart; and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.

weeks.title: Building God’s System
weeks.theme: Let your Kingdom come; the ultimate purpose of love and marriage is to glorify God and build a household that belongs to God.
group: What are the three petitions in Matt 6:9–10? Which one most needs to be fulfilled first in your life?
This past year, where did I see my own self-centeredness, and where did I see God’s grace?
In the coming year, how will I build God’s system together with my companions? Ask your group members to pray for one another.
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday service, together with your small group, each say: “My biggest change this year is…” and then pray the Lord’s Prayer together. Finally, send one sentence from today to a friend.
weeks.weekend: This weekend, spend a half day of “thanksgiving and sending” with your companions: look back over the fifty-two weeks, each share three things you are thankful for, each write down one thing to practice in the coming year, lay hands on one another and pray, and give the glory to Jesus.

lessons.title: May Your Name Be Honored as Holy
lessons.hear:
Xiaoxin had just ended a relationship. She opened the Lord’s Prayer and meditated on it line by line, and when she reached may your name be honored as holy, tears ran down her face. She said: This past year I put many people and things ahead of God, and now I want to honor God’s name as holy first.

Jesus taught us to pray like this: “Let your Kingdom come.” (Matt 6:10) Honor his name as holy, let his Kingdom come, let his will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Three petitions: God’s name, God’s Kingdom, God’s will.

This is the heart of the 3-2-1 ideology: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory, and build God’s system.

It is the same in love: I do not pray in order to get a person, but so that God’s name is honored as holy in my relationships, so that God’s Kingdom comes in me, and so that God’s will is done.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: his whole life honored the Father’s name as holy. The Bible is my standard: God’s name, God’s Kingdom, God’s will. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he makes these three petitions come true in us. Let Jesus be King, and let Jesus receive all the glory. Self says I will be lord; selflessness says your will be done.
think: In Matt 6:9–10, what are the three petitions?
Are my love life and relationships honoring God’s name as holy right now?
Today, how can I let God’s Kingdom come in me, even a little?
lessons.speak: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy. Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Help me honor you as holy first, let Jesus be King, and give all the glory to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, slowly pray the Lord’s Prayer three times, and after each time answer in your heart: “Lord, I am willing.” And write down one small thing you will obey today.
lessons.quick: May God’s name be honored as holy, may his Kingdom come, and may his will be done.
text: Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

lessons.title: The Working of Each Individual Part
lessons.hear:
Jie had always felt that he was just an ordinary person who didn’t stand out at church. Then one time in the small group, everyone was tidying up the space together, and he was in charge of setting out chairs. The group leader said that without him, nobody could have sat down today. For the first time he felt that he had a place in the body.

Paul says: “but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ, from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.” (Eph 4:15–16)

Every person has a “working” that fits. Some are suited to lead, some to accompany, some to prepare, some to pray. There is no higher or lower, only each doing their own part.

In building God’s system, every selfless person is an indispensable joint.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he is the head, and he also serves the body. The Bible is my standard: speak the truth in love, each doing their own part and helping one another. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives all kinds of gifts so that the body is built up in love. A person ruled by self compares which working is higher or lower; a person living in selflessness does their own part and helps others to be complete.
think: According to Eph 4:16, how does the body grow?
Do I compare my role with others’, or look down on my own?
Right now, what small thing can I do for someone in the body?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, you are the head, and we are the members. Help me not to compare and not to feel inferior, but to be faithful in the place you have arranged for me. Help me speak the truth in love, to help my brothers and sisters, and to build up your body in love. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, take the initiative to do one small thing for the fellowship or small group (set out chairs, send a caring message, prepare tea), not to be seen, but only to serve the body.
lessons.quick: Every selfless person is an indispensable joint in the body.
text: but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ,

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.

lessons.title: The Invitation to the Wedding Supper of the Lamb
lessons.hear:
At a wedding, a single sister was asked: When will it be your turn? She smiled and said that she had already received the greatest invitation.

Revelation says: “Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.” (Rev 19:9) This is the end of history, and the hope of the gospel: Christ and his church will be united forever. Single or married, the qualification for being invited is the same: through the blood of the Lamb, to be clothed in the righteous acts of the saints (Rev 19:8).

This reminds us that marriage on earth is a shadow, and Christ and the church are the reality. Some marry and some stay single; each of us is invited to the grandest wedding feast of all.

So we need not be anxious, and we need not be proud, because our hope is in the Lamb.

May we all hold this hope and rejoice and be glad.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he is the bridegroom who gave himself up for the bride. The Bible is my standard: blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he prepares the bride and lets us hold this hope. A person ruled by self is anxious over the gap in front of them; a person living in selflessness rejoices and is glad toward the eternal wedding feast.
think: According to Rev 19:9, who is blessed?
Right now, is my hope mainly in people, or in the wedding supper of the Lamb?
Today, what is one thing I can do to prepare myself to meet the Lord when he comes?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for inviting me to the wedding supper of the Lamb. Keep me from feeling inferior because I am single, and from being proud because of a relationship. Prepare me, so that I live every day in hope, waiting for your return. Let us rejoice and be glad, and give the glory to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, write a “hope list”: write down three things you look forward to experiencing in eternity, read them aloud to a companion, and pray together for the Lord’s return.
lessons.quick: Single or married, we are all invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.

lessons.title: Go and Make Disciples of All Nations
lessons.hear:
After one gathering, Ming said: I’ve learned so much, but I don’t know where to go and do it. An elder asked him just one question: Who around you lately doesn’t yet know Jesus?

Before ascending, Jesus said to his disciples: “Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” (Matt 28:19–20)

This is the Great Commission, and it is the mission of every one of us. “Go” does not have to mean going far away; it can also mean going to a neighbor. A “disciple” is not an audience member, but someone who follows Jesus.

The last sentence matters most: “I am with you always.” We do not go in our own strength, but because Jesus is with us.

So there is no need to be afraid, only to obey.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he sent out his disciples, and he is with them. The Bible is my standard: go, make disciples of all nations, teaching them to observe. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives power so that we can be witnesses. A person ruled by self fears failure and does not go; a person living in selflessness goes because Jesus is with them. I also hope you will live out this mission.
think: In the last sentence of Matt 28:20, what promise does Jesus give?
Who around me can I go to with the gospel and walk beside?
How can I start with one small action?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for sending me and for promising to be with me. Give me courage to love the people around me and to share the gospel with them. Help me rely not on myself but only on your presence, so that people become your disciples. And help me live out my mission every day. Amen.
lessons.do: Today, pray for a friend who does not yet know Jesus, and send a simple message of care, without preaching, only expressing care. If he is willing, arrange a time to meet.
lessons.quick: Go, and make disciples, because Jesus is with us and we do not go in our own strength.

lessons.title: To the One Who Overcomes, I Will Give a Seat With Me
lessons.hear:
On this last day, we look back over the fifty-two weeks: we set out from “love comes from God,” and passed through ideas, life, daily living, relationships, and ministry, all the way to here. You may already have changed, or you may still be on the road. That’s all right; God’s grace is enough.

Jesus says: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.” (Rev 3:21) This is a promise: to sit with Christ on his throne, reigning together, forever.

Overcoming does not mean that I am stronger than others, but that I live in selflessness and let Jesus live in me. Humility overcomes pride, and selflessness overcomes Satan; our failed lives become victorious lives.

The end of this year is a new beginning: let Jesus be King, give the glory to God, and build God’s system.
lessons.light: This year’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example, the Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide; let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory; build God’s system. Self becomes selflessness, and failure becomes victory. The 9-2-0 practice: practice living in selflessness and bear the nine fruits of the Spirit; the 2-3-5 team: companions, spiritual parents and children, and comrades, together moving toward the great revival of the last days and welcoming the Lord’s return.
think: This past year, where did I see my own self-centeredness?
In Rev 3:21, what promise do those who overcome receive?
How did God sustain me this year? What is the first thing I will do in the coming year?
lessons.speak: Father, thank you for your leading and grace this year. Help me continue in selflessness, let Jesus live in me, and let Jesus be King. Help me build God’s system together with my companions until the Lord returns. All glory, honor, and power belong to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal, write down: my biggest change this year, one person I am thankful for, and one thing to practice in the coming year. Then give the glory to God: pray it aloud, and send it to a companion.
lessons.quick: Overcoming is not being stronger than others, but living in selflessness and letting Jesus live in me.
